Final Arbiter Verdict

This synthesizes the four contested fields. The verdict separates what the evidence can decide from what it cannot, and — where it can — names the stronger position with its caveats.

1. Scoreboard by question (not by religion)

QuestionStronger positionConfidenceWhy
Is the NT's early text recoverable?Christian (reliability)High5,800+ Greek MSS; early attestation; variants traceable because of abundance
Is the NT letter-perfect / unaltered?CriticHighA few weighty passages (Comma Johanneum, Mark 16:9–20, John 7:53–8:11) are demonstrably later; conceded by Christian scholars
Was the Qur'an's rasm fixed very early?Muslim (early stability)HighBirmingham + early hijazi MSS match ʿUthmanic rasm
Has the Qur'an reached us with zero variation?CriticHighSanaa lower text + canonical qiraʾat are physical/internal counter-evidence
Is the Bible wholesale fabricated (strong tahrif)?Defense (charge fails)HighManuscript evidence refutes it; not even the Qur'an's most natural claim
Does the symmetry test favor either side?NeitherHighAn even corruption standard wounds both "perfect preservation" claims about equally
Which text directly states its monotheology?*Qur'an → strict tawhid***HighExplicit; internally consistent on its own terms
Is the Trinity a flat contradiction?Christian (charge fails)Medium–HighEssence/person distinction blocks "1=3"; but rests on contested metaphysics
Is the Trinity explicitly stated in the Bible?CriticHighIt is a cumulative post-biblical synthesis; best single proof-text is spurious

2. The three demanded verdict styles, combined

Present (both best cases). Each chapter states the strongest honest form of both sides — not the strawman.

Weigh (strong / weak / contested).

  • Empirically strong & cross-conceded: NT recoverability; early Qur'anic rasm; NT not letter-perfect; Qur'an not variant-free; strong revisionism is weak; bare "1=3" objection fails.
  • Empirically weak: "the Bible was wholesale fabricated"; "the Qur'an has literally zero variants"; "the Trinity is stated plainly in Scripture"; "the Trinity is a self-evident logical contradiction."
  • Genuinely contested: classical Muslim consensus on nass vs. maʿna; the meaning of Q 5:116's triad; high vs. escalating early Christology; which Trinitarian model (Latin / Social / relative-identity) is best.

Judge (name the stronger side where warranted).

  1. Transmission: symmetric. Both scriptures are early and substantively recoverable; neither is the letter-perfect, variant- free object its popular apologists claim. The corruption debate is almost always "won" by whoever is permitted an asymmetric standard — to which no one is entitled. Net: a draw on the honest standard.
  2. *The tahrif charge specifically: the strong form (Bible fabricated) fails; the weak form (Bible humanly transmitted, variant-bearing, partly composite) succeeds — and is conceded by Christianity itself, which redefines "preservation" as recoverability. Applied evenly, the weak form also* lands on the Qur'an.
  3. Monotheism vs. Trinity — textual: on its own text, the Qur'an wins decisively for stating its theology explicitly and consistently. The Bible is two-stranded; the Trinity is the better synthesis of all its data than strict unitarianism is, but it is constructed, not stated. So: clarity → Qur'an; richness/tension → Bible.
  4. Monotheism vs. Trinity — logic: strict monotheism is simpler and not contradictory. The Trinity is not a formal contradiction but is metaphysically heavy and internally contested. Advantage on parsimony → strict monotheism; the “irrational” charge → fails.

3. What the arbiter explicitly will not rule

  • Whether God exists, is one, or is triune in reality. (Not a historical/textual question — Methodology §5.)
  • Whether divine revelation ought to be textually simple (favoring the Qur'an's profile) or developed/multi-stranded (the Bible's profile). That is a theological value judgment, not an evidentiary one.
  • Which religion is "true." Out of scope, by design.

4. One-paragraph bottom line

On the historical/textual front the contest is closer to a draw than either camp admits: both scriptures are early and recoverable in substance, and both fall short of the flawless-preservation myth their popular defenders sell — the Bible by visible variants, the Qur'an by suppressed ones. The Muslim tahrif argument succeeds only in its weak, symmetric form (which boomerangs) and fails in its strong form. On the theological front the two scriptures are simply different in kind: the Qur'an is textually unambiguous about strict monotheism, while the Bible is textually layered, with the Trinity as a coherent- but-constructed synthesis rather than a stated doctrine. The bare charge that the Trinity is irrational fails; the charge that it is not plainly biblical succeeds. Beyond that line, the questions stop being historical — and so does the arbiter's authority.

This concludes the core textual & logical inquiry (Part I). The study continues with Part II — The Nature of God and Part III — Chronology (creation → end).
